sources.entry: Movie Monad - Desktop video player built with Haskell that uses GStreamer and GTK+.

summary.one_liner: Movie Monad is a free, lightweight desktop video player written in Haskell that uses GStreamer and GTK+ to play local files and web streams.
summary.what_it_does: Plays video files from disk and streams videos from URLs (file:// and web links, opened via the file open button or the command line). Provides play/pause, seek, repeat, slow-down and speed-up playback, and subtitle on/off with language selection. Volume can be raised, lowered, or muted, and the video can be made full screen or resized to standard sizes or freely by resizing the window. Keyboard shortcuts cover mute, full screen, show controls, repeat, volume, seek, and play/pause, including media keys. The README describes it as cross platform, with Linux, Mac, and likely Windows support.
use_cases: play local video files on a desktop
stream web videos without a browser
watch lectures at slower or faster speed
play videos from the command line
lightweight media player for Linux or Mac
how_to_run: Linux AppImage: download, mark as executable, and double-click
Arch/pacman: makepkg -sic from the cloned movie-monad repo
Snap: snap install movie-monad && sudo snap connect movie-monad:removable-media
Mac: run movie-monad-mac-install-script.command from the releases page
Haskell developers: stack update && stack setup && stack install alex happy && stack install haskell-gi && stack install
notable: Built in Haskell on GStreamer and GTK+ 3, with responsive video scaling to fill the window
Distributed as AppImage, Arch package, Flatpak, Snap, and a Mac install script
Originated as a video playback proof of concept for the Gifcurry app
Keyboard shortcuts include media keys (AudioPlay, AudioMute, volume keys)
caveats: Requires GTK+ 3.10 or newer and GStreamer 1.0 with base, good, and bad plug-ins (bad >= 1.8) installed
Windows support is described only as 'most likely'
Building from source requires Haskell Stack and GObject Introspection
